newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish central bank interventions knock down zloty.
newsitem.headline: Polish central bank interventions knock down zloty.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland pulled the rug out from under the zloty on Monday by purchasing dollars and marks on the domestic forex market, dealers said.

Dealers said the intervention, the NBP's first in eight months, drained an estimated $30-$40 million and 10 million German marks. They said it would likely stop the zloty's bull-run for today but not keep it down in the near-term.
"The intervention was small, but it was a signal that the central bank doesn't want the zloty to float more than four percent from the central parity rate," a foreign bank dealer in Warsaw said.
Dealers said the central bank interventions came in three waves, the second of which sent the still perky zloty reeling towards three percent from the parity rate.
The zlotys' bullish mood was spurred by foreign investor entry into Polish treasuries. Dealers estimated foreign entry at today's primary T-bill auction at about 100 million zlotys.
At 1240 GMT the zloty was at 3.34/3.23 percent from parity, or at 2.9470/00 to the dollar and at 1.8050/80 to the mark against 2.9200/20 and 1.8003/13 respectively.
